newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers posts strong year profit rise.
newsitem.headline: De Beers posts strong year profit rise.

text.p: Diamond giant De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd posted strong year results on Tuesday as its earnings per share rose to 354 U.S. cents from 259 cents.
The group also increased its dividend by 10.5 percent to 102.7 U.S. cents a share.
Analysts had expected a good set of results following on from a sparkling performance at the half year in August.
Market watchers say diamond demand is strong and the firm is also reaping benefits from its investments in other firms like Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and Minorco.
In a brief statement De Beers said its combined diamond account for 1996 was $803 million, compared to $780 million in 1995.
The firm's 1996 combined earnings, including a share of retained associates' earnings, were $1,344 million, up fom $986 million.
They included an exceptional profit of $109 million from the disposal of a portion of its interest in industrial holding firm Johnnic.
The group made no comment on the status of talks with Russia on signing a new marketing deal for that country's diamonds.
De Beers shares rose after the news was announced to a new year high of 159.75 cents.
